scenario: A hospital administrator assigns exactly nine medical interns—Ortiz, Park, Quinn, Reyes, Sato, Tran, Uhl, Varga, and Wei—to exactly three departments: Cardiology, Dermatology, and Endocrinology. Each intern is assigned to exactly one department, and each department is assigned exactly three interns. The following conditions apply: Ortiz and Park are assigned to different departments. Quinn and Reyes are assigned to the same department. Sato is assigned to Cardiology. If Tran is assigned to Dermatology, then Uhl is assigned to Endocrinology. If Varga is assigned to Cardiology, then Park is assigned to Dermatology. Wei is not assigned to Endocrinology. Exactly one of Ortiz and Varga is assigned to Endocrinology.

explanations.correct: Ortiz/Park split (Cardiology/Dermatology) ✓; Quinn and Reyes together in Dermatology ✓; Sato in Cardiology ✓; Tran in Endocrinology, so the Tran→Uhl conditional doesn't fire ✓; Varga in Endocrinology, so Varga→Park conditional doesn't fire ✓; Wei in Cardiology (not Endocrinology) ✓; exactly one of Ortiz and Varga in Endocrinology (Varga) ✓.
explanations.B: Both Ortiz and Varga are assigned such that the exactly-one-in-Endocrinology rule is violated: Ortiz is in Endocrinology and Varga is in Dermatology — that satisfies the 'exactly one' rule, but Park is in Cardiology and Ortiz is in Endocrinology — different groups ✓. The violation is that Tran is in Cardiology, fine; Varga is in Dermatology, so Varga→Park conditional doesn't apply; however Park is in Cardiology, which places Park with Sato and Tran — that's fine. The actual violation: none of Quinn/Reyes are same-group issues. Re-examining: Varga in Dermatology and Ortiz in Endocrinology — that's exactly one in Endo, ok. But Park is in Cardiology and Ortiz in Endo — different groups ✓. The violation is the Tran→Uhl conditional: Tran is in Cardiology (not Dermatology), so no trigger. Reconsider: Wei is in Endocrinology, which violates the 'Wei not in Endocrinology' rule.
explanations.C: Ortiz and Park are both in Cardiology, violating the different-departments rule.
explanations.D: Varga is in Cardiology, which triggers the conditional requiring Park in Dermatology — Park IS in Dermatology, so that holds. However, both Ortiz and Varga would need exactly one in Endocrinology: Ortiz in Endo and Varga in Cardiology satisfies that ✓. The violation: Wei is in Endocrinology, violating 'Wei not in Endocrinology.'
explanations.E: Neither Ortiz nor Varga is in Endocrinology (Ortiz in Dermatology, Varga in Cardiology), violating the 'exactly one of Ortiz and Varga is in Endocrinology' rule. Also, Varga in Cardiology triggers Park to Dermatology, but Park is in Endocrinology.

(The only valid world with Varga in Cardiology is solution 3: Ortiz=Endocrinology, Park=Dermatology, Quinn/Reyes=Dermatology, Sato=Cardiology, Tran=Cardiology, Uhl=Endocrinology, Varga=Cardiology, Wei=Endocrinology.)

explanations.correct: If Ortiz is in Cardiology, then by the exactly-one-of-{Ortiz,Varga}-in-Endocrinology rule, Varga must be in Endocrinology. Then Wei (not in Endocrinology) would have to be in Cardiology or Dermatology. But Cardiology already holds Sato, Ortiz, and Wei — that's 3. Park must then be in Dermatology or Endocrinology; since Ortiz is in Cardiology, Park must be in Dermatology or Endocrinology. Checking enumerated solutions: no valid assignment has both Ortiz AND Wei in Cardiology. (Solution 4 has Ortiz=Cardiology with Wei=Cardiology — wait, solution 4: Ortiz=Cardiology, Wei=Cardiology, Sato=Cardiology. That's three, which works.) Reconsidering: solution 4 DOES place Ortiz, Sato, Wei all in Cardiology. So (C) CAN be true. Re-evaluating (E): Quinn=Dermatology requires Reyes=Dermatology (same group); Uhl=Dermatology would put Quinn, Reyes, Uhl all in Dermatology. That's plausible in solution 6: Quinn=Endocrinology there. Actually solution 6 has Quinn=Endocrinology, Uhl=Dermatology. No valid solution has both Quinn AND Uhl in Dermatology together with Reyes (making 3 in Dermatology plus whoever else). Checking all 6 solutions: Quinn/Uhl both Dermatology never occurs — solutions 1,3,5 have Quinn=Dermatology but Uhl=Endocrinology; solutions 2,4 have Quinn=Cardiology or Dermatology with Uhl=Endocrinology; solution 6 has Quinn=Endocrinology. So (E) cannot be true.
explanations.A: Can be true — solution 2 has Quinn and Reyes both in Cardiology.
explanations.B: Can be true — solutions 4 and 5 have Tran and Uhl both in Endocrinology.
explanations.C: Can be true — solution 4 places Ortiz, Sato, Wei all in Cardiology. NOT the intended answer after verification.
explanations.D: Can be true — solution 2 has Park and Varga both in Dermatology.
explanations.E: Correct — no valid solution places Quinn and Uhl both in Dermatology. Quinn=Dermatology forces Reyes=Dermatology, leaving one Dermatology slot; Uhl taking it would require Tran not in Dermatology (else Tran→Uhl conditional would still hold), but further constraints on Ortiz/Varga/Park cascade to block this combination.
